== Biography ==
Agnes Glasgow is represented by the Kirknewton and East Calder births/baptisms index entry dated 28 February 1677, which names her father as Alexander Glasgow. The indexed date is not independently established as her birthday. [[Glasgow-3118|Alexander Glasgow]], the local man indexed marrying Margaret Smith in 1667, is her probable father (83% subjective research confidence); the identification is inferred from the parish household sequence. [[Smith-230509|Margaret Smith]] remains an unproved mother. The existing structured father already identifies Glasgow-3118; the former biography link to Glasgow-1152 was stale.

=== Kirknewton household review,21 October 2026 ===
Agnes’s 28 February 1677 Kirknewton/East Calder index names father Alexander Glasgow. The same-parish Alexander married Margaret Smith on 18 October 1667; Alexander’s 1673 child entry and Agnes’s 1677 entry name the same father four years apart. This favours one local household and extends the existing probable father identification across the two children. Assess Alexander Glasgow-3118 as Agnes’s probable father at 83% subjective confidence. The ten-year marriage-to-Agnes interval leaves somewhat more room for a second household than the six-year interval for Alexander-1314, whose existing 85% is unchanged. The parish index supplies no mother, occupation, precise residence or explicit link to the 1667 groom. Another Alexander remains possible. The children’s existing tree sibling link is not independent corroboration. The saved confident father flag is retained as capture provenance, not adopted as an independently verified grade. Margaret Smith’s maternity remains unproved and is not upgraded or transferred to another child. No birth/death date, parent identity, sibling topology or upstream father changes.

Do not treat the stale Glasgow-1152 link as independent evidence that the adults are one man. The 1665 Edinburgh Alexander/Issobell Anderson marriage belongs to the maintained Glasgow-1152 couple. Marie’s 11 October 1674 St Cuthbert’s baptism transcript explicitly names Alexander Glasgow and Issobell Andersone, after the 1667 Kirknewton Margaret Smith marriage and between the 1673 and 1677 Kirknewton children. A simple first-wife-died/remarriage account therefore has an unexplained overlap. The dates are baptism/index dates, so delayed baptism or a more complicated family history cannot be excluded. Prefer separate household accounts pending a record explaining the overlap; no categorical identity exclusion or merge is made.<ref>ScotlandsPeople,OPR690/10/77,Agnes Glasgow,28 February1677,fatherAlexander; supplied index row18,10 September2026. Alexander Glasgow/MargaretSmith marriage,OPR690/10/54,18 October1667,FamilySearch XY9W-TPB. Alexander child,1673,FamilySearch VQ4K-X9V. Marie Glasgow,11 October1674,AlexanderGlasgow/IssobellAndersone,Findmypast [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F0702947&tab=this SCOT/OPR/BAP/0702947],OPR685_2/3 item2,retained transcript; supplied ScotlandsPeople locator685/2,30/86,FR631. Original registers not newly inspected.</ref>

The earlier marriage/banns comparisons remain unproved. Entries in1666 and1670 precede the defining1677 baptism; the1681 entry is only four years later. An adult or delayed baptism is not categorically impossible, but no inspected age, kinship or household detail supports those identifications. They are not used as evidence of her life events or parentage.
